articles.title: Neoadjuvant Immune Checkpoint Blockade in Resectable Melanoma: A Randomized Phase 2 Trial
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors improve outcomes in advanced cancer, but their role before surgery is unclear. METHODS: In this randomized phase 2 trial, 120 adults with resectable stage III melanoma received either two cycles of neoadjuvant pembrolizumab followed by surgery (n=60) or surgery followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab (n=60). The primary endpoint was event-free survival at 24 months. RESULTS: Event-free survival at 24 months was 72% in the neoadjuvant group and 54% in the adjuvant group (hazard ratio 0.58; 95% CI 0.36-0.93; P=0.02). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 18% and 15% of patients, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab improved event-free survival compared with adjuvant therapy, with similar toxicity.
references: Demo A et al. Adjuvant therapy in melanoma. J Demo Med. 2021.
Sample B et al. PD-1 blockade and survival. Demo Lancet. 2022.

articles.title: Combination CAR-T Cell Therapy and PD-1 Blockade in Relapsed B-Cell Lymphoma: A Single-Arm Study
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Relapse after CAR-T cell therapy is common. METHODS: In this single-arm phase 1/2 study, 45 patients with relapsed or refractory B-cell lymphoma received CAR-T cells followed by PD-1 blockade. The primary endpoint was safety; the secondary endpoint was complete response rate at 3 months. RESULTS: Complete response at 3 months was 58% (26 of 45). Cytokine release syndrome of grade 3 or higher occurred in 9% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The combination was feasible and showed encouraging activity; randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors and Immune-Related Adverse Events: A Systematic Review
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are a major limitation of checkpoint inhibitor therapy. METHODS: We searched three databases and included 38 studies with 9,412 patients. RESULTS: Any-grade irAEs occurred in 66% of patients on combination therapy and 27% on PD-1 monotherapy. Colitis and hepatitis were the most frequent serious events. CONCLUSIONS: Combination regimens carry substantially higher toxicity, and early recognition is important.
